subject: Open-model trial proposal: parity gates, recommended models, and prompt bundles
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Knox <samuel.knox@fidelityedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed trial plan (open models vs baseline)

Sam — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a short trial spun up next week.

Key takeaways: \n- Primary scoring goal: document classification accuracy on regulatory doc set (precision prioritized over recall). \n- Latency target for inference in-prod: 150ms p95 for single-shot classification. \n- Data sensitivity: no PHI, but strictly regulated PII handling and retention controls required.

Proposed trial plan (2 weeks):
1) Baseline: run your current proprietary ensemble on a 1k doc holdout you shared (we'll accept your hashed IDs).
2) Open-model candidates: run three model variants we recommend (see below) on the same holdout and compare metrics and failure modes.
3) Acceptance gates: define parity thresholds (see attached brief) — primary gate = F1 parity >= 0.97 of baseline on priority classes; secondary gate = no >3x increase in high-confidence false positives for any class.
4) Prompt bundle: start with the attached prompt bundle (short, templated instructions + 6 example edge-case prompts); we'll iterate after the first run.

Recommended open models (initial shortlist):
- LlamaX-13B-q4f: best latency/cost trade-off for short classification.
- Falcon-40B-instruct-8bit: stronger on rare classes in our benchmarks but higher mem footprint.
- Redstone-7B-tuned: Redwood-verified, lower-cost quantized variant that often matches baseline on conversational-to-structured tasks.

Attachments: fidelityedge-trial-prompt-bundle-v1.json, parity-thresholds-brief.pdf, trial-setup-runbook.md

Asks: can you confirm the holdout bucket (hash prefix or S3 path) and whether your security team needs an NDA addendum for the trial infra? If yes, loop your legal contact and we can get a limited-scope DPA queued.

I can schedule the initial run once you confirm — proposed kickoff Monday 13th at 10am PT for a 30-minute sync.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai
From: Samuel Knox <samuel.knox@fidelityedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@fidelityedge.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed trial plan (open models vs baseline)

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: \n- We can provide the 1k hashed holdout as an S3 path (s3://fe-prod-trials/fid4837/holdout-1k) by COB Monday.
- Legal: no additional NDA needed for this trial, but our security team will need an architecture diagram and a short list of data handling controls (encryption at rest/in transit, KMS usage, audit log retention).
- Priority classes: Regulatory_Filing, Customer_Consent, Account_Open.

On acceptance gates — F1 parity >= 0.97 sounds reasonable as a starting point, but Priya (cc) asked whether we can also include per-class minimum thresholds (e.g., Reg_Filing F1 >= 0.95).

We're happy to kick off Monday 13th at 10am PT. Please include an agenda and the runbook link in the calendar invite.

Best,
Sam
Senior Product Manager, FidelityEdge

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Knox <samuel.knox@fidelityedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed trial plan (open models vs baseline)

Sam — great, thank you. Agenda + runbook links below and short note on per-class gates.

Agenda (30m kickoff):
- 0–5m: Introductions + success criteria confirmation
- 5–10m: Security checklist (Marissa) + trial infra overview
- 10–20m: Trial execution plan (Ben) — data handoff, tempo, and outputs
- 20–30m: Next steps, reporting cadence, success/rollback criteria

Per-class gates suggestion: we recommend the following initial thresholds (see attached PDF for rationale):
- Regulatory_Filing: F1 >= 0.95
- Customer_Consent: F1 >= 0.96
- Account_Open: F1 >= 0.94

Benchmark links and notes:
- Open-model benchmark dashboard (internal): https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmark/open-model-benchmarks#fidelityedge (contains standardized prompts and latency/cost sims)
- Public benchmark paper we referenced: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01234 (sec 4 discusses short-context classification behavior)

Prompt bundle (attached): file fidelityedge-trial-prompt-bundle-v1.json includes:
- 12 templated instructions: short few-shot examples and targeted edge-case prompts for the three priority classes
- Scoring rubric for confidence calibration and post-hoc thresholding suggestions

Ben will take point on the initial run and upload results to the Drive folder (link in runbook). For the architecture diagram and controls: Marissa will share a short one-pager in the security doc during the kickoff.

Next steps (action owners):
- Sam/Priya: confirm S3 path and share contact for security review (by EOD Mon)
- Ben: prepare run script and initial run container (will be ready for kickoff)
- Marissa: prepare security controls one-pager and list of logs/audit retention

I'll send the calendar invite with the agenda + links now. Looking forward to it.

Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: fidelityedge-trial-prompt-bundle-v1.json, parity-thresholds-brief.pdf, trial-setup-runbook.md
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Knox <samuel.knox@fidelityedge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed trial plan (open models vs baseline)

Sam — quick technical note before kickoff:
- I'll provision an isolated trial cluster (ephemeral VPC) in us-west-2 and mount the S3 holdout read-only. No customer data will be persisted beyond the trial window; artifacts will be hashed and stored in the runbook folder.
- Container image: redwood/trial-runner:20260713 (includes the three model adapters and our evaluation harness).
- Expected outputs after run (zipped): metrics.csv (per-class precision/recall/F1 plus calibration stats), error-samples.jsonl (50 examples per class flagged as high-confidence errors), latency_report.json, and raw_inference_log.ndjson (hashed ids only).

I uploaded the runbook and a stub architecture diagram to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_trial_runbook — you'll find the step-by-step there. If Priya or your security team want a short call with Marissa and our infra lead, we can add a 15-minute pre-kickoff slot.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
